info.title: grid-aware
info.description: Combined global (Electricity Maps) and UK-regional (NESO) grid carbon intensity API.

zone.description: Electricity Maps zone code (always "GB" for NESO responses).

unknown.description: True when none of id/name/nation could be determined for this request.

region.description: GB DNO region detail, when known. id/name are only ever present for NESO regional responses; nation may be present on its own when only a coarser signal (e.g. Cloudflare's detected nation) was available.

location.description: Echoes back where this response is about, so you never have to re-parse the request.

datetime.description: Start of the reporting period, ISO 8601 UTC.

validTo.description: End of the reporting period, when known.

value.description: The carbon intensity figure, in `unit`. `null` when `band` is "unknown".

type.description: "actual" = measured (NESO national, when available), "forecast" = NESO's forward estimate (national fallback and all regional data), "estimated" = Electricity Maps' modeled figure (or its annual average, for CO2.js fallbacks), "unknown" = an upstream provider failed or returned unusable data.

band.description: Coarse category for the value. GB responses use NESO's own index (recalculated by NESO each year against GB's own grid); other zones use generic, approximate global thresholds since no equivalent official index exists worldwide. "unknown" means an upstream provider failed or returned unusable data, see `fallback.reason`.

generationMix.description: Fuel mix behind this figure. Only returned for NESO regional responses.

forecast.description: Near-future periods covering the requested horizon window (NESO: 30-minute periods; Electricity Maps: hourly), including the period already summarized above. Present only when `horizon` is "24h" or "48h", and never for CO2.js fallbacks.

attribution.description: Credits for each source used in this response. Keep them with the data if you display or redistribute it.

fallback.description: Present when a GB request was redirected from NESO to Electricity Maps because the caller wasn't UK-origin, or when the intended upstream provider failed. Failures fall back from NESO to Electricity Maps' GB zone, then to Electricity Maps' latest annual average via CO2.js (`source: "co2js"`), and only report `band`/`type` as "unknown" if the zone isn't in that dataset either.

datetime.description: Start of this period, ISO 8601 UTC.

validTo.description: End of this period, when known.

value.description: The carbon intensity figure, in `unit`. `null` when `band` is "unknown".

band.description: Coarse category for the value. GB responses use NESO's own index (recalculated by NESO each year against GB's own grid); other zones use generic, approximate global thresholds since no equivalent official index exists worldwide. "unknown" means an upstream provider failed or returned unusable data, see `fallback.reason`.

generationMix.description: Fuel mix for this period. Only present for NESO regional forecasts.

surplus.description: MW at the day's peak half hour.

bmrs.description: NESO's National Surplus Forecast from Elexon BMRS (OCNMFD). GB-wide. Omitted if BMRS is unavailable.

percentageOfDemand.description: Surplus as a % of forecast national demand (BMRS NDFD). Absent when there's no demand forecast for the day.

windPercentageOfCapacity.description: Average forecast wind output as a % of wind capacity (NESO 14-day wind forecast). Transmission-connected wind only. Absent for part-days.

dayRank.description: Rank for running deferrable compute, 1 being best. Days with spare capacity (`surplus` above 0) come first, so extra load doesn't land on a grid short of capacity. Then wind share, as a stand-in for lower carbon this far ahead; days within 5 percentage points of each other (e.g. 60% and 65%) count as equal, as the forecast isn't that precise. Then higher `percentageOfDemand`, since the same spare MW is more headroom on a quieter day (raw MW if there's no demand forecast). Then the earlier date, so no two days share a rank.

renewablePercentage.description: Wind + solar + hydro share of the region's current mix, as a %.

regional.description: A proxy, not a measured surplus. Regional responses only.

from.description: ISO 8601 UTC. May be the start of the current period.

window.description: Lowest average intensity window in the next 48 hours that fits the job length from `surplus`. Earliest wins a tie.

derived.description: Calculated by grid-aware, not published by NESO or Elexon.

text.example: Contains BMRS data © Elexon Limited copyright and database right 2026
text.description: Credit required by the source's licence or terms.

start.description: When to start the job, ISO 8601 UTC. The current time when no better time is known.

end.description: End of the suggested window. Absent when `start` is the current time and there is no window.

averageIntensity.description: Average carbon intensity over the window, in `unit`.

durationMinutes.description: The job length the window was sized for.

withinBand.description: Only present when `band` was asked for. True if every period in the window is at or below that band; false if none was, and the window is the cleanest one instead.

attribution.description: Credits for each source used in this response. Keep them with the data if you display or redistribute it.

fallback.description: Present when `start` is the current time because no window could be worked out, such as when the forecast was unavailable.

get.description: Routes to NESO for GB and to Electricity Maps for everything else. Defaults to Cloudflare-detected location (postcode or city).

schema.description: Electricity Maps zone code. If omitted along with postcode/regionid, defaults to the caller's own location as detected by Cloudflare (a UK postcode where available, else the caller's country).

schema.description: Adds `surplus` to GB (NESO) responses. Pass a job length in minutes (max 2880) to size `surplus.derived.suggested.window`, or "true" for 30.

get.description: The start of the lowest-intensity window in the next 48 hours that is long enough for the job, optionally limited to starting within a number of minutes. Works for every zone. When no window can be worked out it returns the current time with a `fallback` reason.
